title: Update hosted benchmark narratives + performance transparency guidance for FP8/INT8 sprint outcomes
creator: Henry Cho
description: PM task to update internal/external benchmark narratives: what can be claimed, how to footnote, and which models/SKUs get updated charts.
content:
## Context
We’re landing meaningful FP8/INT8 runtime improvements (kernel dispatch + scheduler tuning) and will be asked by customers/prospects for “numbers” (especially H100) and clarity on *what those numbers mean*.

We need a single, consistent performance-transparency package that:
- Is defensible and reproducible (methodology + variance + environment pinning).
- Clearly distinguishes microbench vs end-to-end serving benchmarks.
- Avoids over-claiming (esp. when the win is workload-dependent or requires specific scheduler knobs).
- States what changed (kernel mode defaults, eligibility rules, fallbacks) without exposing internal-only details.

This ticket owns the narrative + claim boundaries, not the underlying benchmark execution.

## Goals
1) Define what we can claim internally and externally for the FP8/INT8 sprint results (latency/throughput/cost proxy), including required footnotes.
2) Decide which hosted models + GPU SKUs get updated charts for the next performance transparency refresh.
3) Provide enablement materials for Sales/Solutions/CS: pre-approved excerpts, caveats, and a Q&A.

## Non-goals
- Producing the benchmark numbers (owned by runtime + evals). We only consume approved aggregates.
- Changing kernel-selection behavior (owned by ENG ADR/implementation).

## Inputs / reference links
- Benchmark methodology + interpretation:
  - sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-benchmarking-methodology-top-hosted-models.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/benchmarking-standards-fp8-int8.json
- Quality / quantization policy constraints:
  - sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/fp8-int8-profile-policy-for-hosted-catalog.json
- Working results artifacts (for internal review only):
  - sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/fp8-int8-benchmark-matrix-v1.json
  - sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/quality-vs-quantization-evals-summary.json
- Alignment thread (source of truth for claim boundaries):
  - sources/gmail/irene_choi/20260218-performance-transparency-what-we-can-claim.json

## Proposed updated chart coverage (v1)
### GPU SKUs
- H100 (primary, most requested)
- A100 (enterprise baseline)
- L4 (cost-focused SKU; only if we have clean + stable runs for at least 2 representative models)

### Models (hosted top traffic + common customer asks)
Proposed “Top 6 hosted models” set to align with ENG matrix runner coverage. Pending final sign-off from Talia Benson + Hiro Tanaka based on what’s complete and stable.

Selection criteria:
- Meaningful traffic share on hosted.
- Representative of different shapes (hidden size/head dims) so results aren’t overfit.
- Has passing quality sanity under the recommended quant profile.

## Claim boundaries (draft)
### Allowed claims (external, with footnotes)
- “Up to X% improvement” only when we can show:
  - Multiple workloads (at least 2 of: short prompts, medium prompts, mixed prefill/decode) AND
  - Stable variance (per standards) AND
  - Clear definition of metric (e.g., p95 TTFT, p95 TPOT, tokens/s at steady state).

- Prefer phrasing:
  - “In our hosted-like benchmark suite” rather than “in production for all workloads.”
  - “H100 improvements are larger than A100 in these regimes” (when supported) but avoid implying parity across all SKUs.

### Disallowed / avoid
- Single-number blanket claim across “all prompts” or “all workloads.”
- Claiming “cost reduction” unless tied to a clear proxy + assumptions (token throughput at fixed utilization, or $/1M tokens under fixed batch/concurrency).
- Publishing microbench-only results as end-to-end wins.

### Required footnotes (external)
- Hardware + software pinning: GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, runtime version.
- Workload definition: prompt length distribution, decode length, concurrency, batching policy.
- Metric definition: TTFT, TPOT, tokens/sec, and the percentiles reported.
- Variance + run count: minimum N runs, observed variance band, and any excluded outliers policy.
- Quantization caveat: quality may vary by workload; link to guidance on evaluation / fallback behavior.

## Deliverables
1) **Performance Transparency Guidance (internal)**
   - One pager: “What we can claim” + required footnotes + example approved language.
   - Includes a “safe phrasing” and “don’t say this” section.

2) **Chart inclusion list**
   - Final list of models + SKUs to update.
   - For each, specify which metrics we will show (TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s) and which workloads.

3) **Customer-facing enablement**
   - Sales/Solutions pre-approved excerpts (2–3 variants: short email response, deck slide text, technical appendix blurb).
   - FAQ stubs: FP8 vs INT8 differences, quality concerns, rollout/canary safety, how to run a pilot benchmark.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stakeholder sign-off: Henry Cho (PM), Jonas Weber (Evals), Rafael Mendes (SRE) that claims/footnotes are accurate and not misleading.
- [ ] Final “models + SKUs + workloads” coverage list posted in #eng-runtime and #sales-eng enablement channel.
- [ ] Approved language integrated into PM-1186 customer comms template (or linked with clear “use this” guidance).
- [ ] Includes explicit guidance on when we must defer to a customer-specific pilot benchmark (e.g., long-context, tool-calling heavy, highly structured output workloads).

## Open questions
1) L4 coverage: do we have enough stable runs to publish anything non-misleading? If not, keep L4 internal-only for now.
2) Long-context regimes: we likely need stronger caveats (quality + performance variance). If we include, must be clearly labeled.
3) Default policy timing: if runtime defaults aren’t globally enabled, we need to state “available behind flags / rolling out by region/model cohort.”

## Risks
- Oversimplifying results and creating a support burden when customer workloads don’t match the benchmark mix.
- Publishing numbers before perf canary thresholds are stable (risk of immediate revision).
- Quality concerns for INT8 on summarization/search: must include “eval sign-off required” guidance.

## Next steps
- Aditya: incorporate feedback from Irene thread + Jonas sign-off criteria into the one-pager draft.
- Henry: confirm which charts are needed for external refresh vs internal-only.
- Sync with Talia on matrix completeness; do not lock the coverage list until the “variance-clean” set is known.
comments: 2026-02-12 (Henry Cho): Kicked this off after Summit AI asked for “H100 FP8 vs INT8 numbers” + timing. Goal is to avoid a one-off answer and standardize what we share. Looping in Jonas for sign-off criteria and Irene for footnote policy.

2026-02-18 (Aditya Rao): Drafted claim boundaries + footnotes based on Irene’s email. Main callout: do not translate to “cost reduction” without explicit assumptions; stick to TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s under defined workload mix. Pending Jonas review of quantization caveats.

2026-02-21 (Jonas Weber): Quality caveat must be front-and-center. For INT8, require either (a) customer-specific eval on their prompt set or (b) Redwood sanity suite + no regressions in long-context slice. OK to say “INT8 can be workload-dependent; fallback available” but avoid “no quality impact.”

2026-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE perspective, external messaging should mention staged rollout + automatic rollback on canary breach. Avoid implying global enablement on day 1. Provide a simple statement: “rollout begins with canary cohorts; expands after stability.”

2026-02-26 (Aditya Rao): Marking In Review. Coverage proposal updated: H100 + A100 for external charts; L4 internal-only unless we get stable runs for 2 models with clean variance. Sent the one-pager draft to Henry/Jonas/Rafael for final sign-off.
